shortDefinition: The type of AI model behind most image and video generation tools.
fullDefinition: Diffusion models are a class of generative AI models that learn to generate images by gradually adding and removing noise. They start with random noise and iteratively 'denoise' it guided by a text description or other input, producing realistic images. Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, and Midjourney are all based on diffusion models. Diffusion models are distinct from LLMs — they work with pixel distributions rather than text tokens.
